subject.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject each OpenAI/Codex image entry above generatedMediaMaxBytes, including making an all-oversized otherwise-valid response fail through the existing missing-image path?
rationale: This is a deliberate security-versus-compatibility boundary: it prevents transient decode allocation but changes the observable result for provider responses that were formerly accepted under only the aggregate JSON limit.

options.title: Accept the per-image fail-closed boundary
options.body: Approve the guard after direct Codex-source verification confirms that partial and empty image-result handling matches the intended upstream contract.

options.title: Keep aggregate-only behavior for OAuth
options.body: Limit the PR to paths with an established per-item limit and leave the Codex/OpenAI OAuth parser under its existing aggregate response cap until a product contract is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept the per-image fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the guard after direct Codex-source verification confirms that partial and empty image-result handling matches the intended upstream contract.
